lines: Here's the whole batch, baker. We didn't start out a little off. Paul says we were "dead in your trespasses and sins," following the ways of this world and the cravings of the flesh (Eph 2:1-3).
And dead means DEAD, friend. A dead guy can't fix his life. He can't even hit the snooze button.

But God, rich in mercy and because of His great love, made us alive with Christ, raised us up and seated us with Him, so in the coming ages He could display "the surpassing riches of His grace" (Eph 2:4-7).
So being saved is grace, through faith. It's the gift of God, not from ourselves and not by works, so no one can boast (Eph 2:8-9).
Think about it. Nobody brags about how hard they worked to open a present.
Then the good works show up, not to earn anything, but because we are God's workmanship, created in Christ Jesus to do good works He prepared in advance (Eph 2:10).
Grace first, works second. Flip that order and you're frosting the cookie before it's even baked. And Paul's not done with this letter yet, friend.
